what: Inside a reading window attached to the screen (from 140px below the header to 40px above the screen bottom), a long text enters from the window’s bottom edge and is bound to scroll, rising until it exits past the top edge (window height + text height, no curve), lines entering the 22% bands at the window’s top and bottom fade toward the edges and blur up to 8px — only the middle lines are sharp. From .35 screen height before the text has fully exited, the title beside it disappears too

options.band: Blurred edge band (ratio of window height), default .22
options.fade: Where the title starts to fade (share of screen height from the end), default .35
options.min: Minimum window width for reveal (px), default 768 — below that the text just flows
options.[data-fx-part=window]: Reading window pinned to the screen — child of the panel
options.[data-fx-part=body]: Block of text scrolling up inside the window
options.[data-fx-part=line]: Per-line span for line-by-line blur — one for each line split by br inside a paragraph
options.[data-fx-part=fade]: (optional) Title that disappears at the end — inside the panel or right beside it

use:
First line
Second row

from.where: index.html .gh-about (About section — intro text over dark video). Original Top about(): reading window sticky top header+40px · height 100svh−header−80px, text y window height → −text height(start top window top, end += Window + text, scrub true), line blur band .22 · 8px, title opacity 1→0 (end − screen .35) → end

note: Sets the panel (el) height to viewport + viewport + text so the viewport stays pinned during that span. It measures line positions every frame, so a very large number of lines (hundreds) is heavy — it only runs while the panel is on screen.
